nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|Resilient infrastructure|Waste management solutions_qna_000
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: Why is waste management considered important in the global agenda?
nodes.answer: Waste management is important in the global agenda because it affects each of the United Nations' triple planetary crises: climate change, nature and biodiversity, and pollution and waste.
nodes.paragraph: Keywords Local knowledge Waste management Sustainable communities Socio-ecological systems framework Integrated sustainable approach Botswana * Isabella P. Ntsabane ipmakgatswana@gmail.com Kgosietsile Velempini velempinik@uncw.edu Hesekia Garekae Garekaeh@ub.ac.bw Pulane Koosaletse-Mswela Mswelap@ub.ac.bw 1 Environmental Education Unit, Languages and Social Science Education Department, Faculty of Education, University of Botswana, Gaborone, Botswana 2 Department of Environmental Sciences, University of North Carolina Wilmington, Wilmington, USA 3 Department of Environmental Science, Faculty of Sciences, University of Botswana, Gaborone, Botswana 4 Department of Range and Forest Resources, Botswana University of Agriculture and Natural Resources, Gaborone, Botswana 58 Socio-Ecological Practice Research (2025) 7:57 76 1 Introduction Waste management has both direct and indirect environ- mental impacts, which include land occupation, resource depletion, global warming, water pollution and cytotoxic effects from air emissions (Parveen et al. 2023, p. ix). Waste is important in the global agenda because it affects each one of the United Nations triple planetary crisis of climate change, nature and biodiversity, and pollution and waste (UNEP 2023, p. 2 of 15).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|Resilient infrastructure|Waste management solutions_qna_001
nodes.question: How does Level 2 of the solutions in Jakarta aim to enhance waste management practices?
nodes.answer: Level 2 of the solutions in Jakarta concentrates on enhancing waste management practices through the 3R concept: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|Resilient infrastructure|Waste management solutions_qna_002
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How can a company improve waste management as part of its business strategy?
nodes.answer: A company can improve waste management by focusing on minimizing risks in waste collection and disposal through the implementation of a new risk evaluation model and the establishment of a project team with expertise in EHS risk assessment and waste management.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|Resilient infrastructure|Waste management solutions_qna_003
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What are some of the costs associated with managing obsolete or dead stock items in terms of waste management?
nodes.answer: The management of obsolete or dead stock items adds to carbon emissions, labour costs, and waste management costs, such as those for incineration or landfilling, which can have a significant impact on a company's bottom line and environmental footprint.
